description: Phase-GRAPH-FULL — substrate that turns Aura's wiki from 'markdown with [[links]]' into a real knowledge graph adaptive to any domain (legal/medical/industrial/research). Inserted between Phase-OUT (closed 2026-05-23 commit 6aabfbda) and Phase-CTX by explicit user decision 2026-05-23: 'senza il grafo tutto il resto è inutile, la base deve essere solida al 100%'. Reference patterns lifted from D:/tmp/graphify (Union-Find 3-pass dedup, edge type vocabulary, audit) and D:/tmp/openhuman (RawEntity intermediate model, alias map short/long resolution, ExtractionAccumulator merge). HARD CONSTRAINT per memory feedback_no_regex_for_nlp: NO regex on prose. Entity recognition + alias generation = LLM. Fuzzy matching = embedding cosine (we already have embedder). String matching = literal substring on KNOWN aliases (not patterns). 5 stories, per-module deep refactor on touch mandatory per CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: Wiki frontmatter aliases: [] + AliasIndex with O(1) lookup
userStories.description: Add Aliases []string field to wiki.Page schema (internal/wiki/schema.go) + YAML parse/serialize roundtrip. Build a new AliasIndex (internal/wiki/alias_index.go) — in-memory map[normalizedAlias]canonicalSlug rebuilt on Store load (warm()) and updated incrementally on every WritePage/DeletePage. Normalization: trim + lowercase + collapse internal whitespace + NFC unicode normalize. Conflict policy: longest alias wins (if 'Codice Civile' and 'Codice' both claim by different slugs, 'Codice Civile' takes precedence for the 'codice civile' lookup). Empty alias rejected at parse time. Expose Store.ResolveAlias(s string) (canonicalSlug string, ok bool) as public API for downstream consumers (GRAPH-02 injection + future graph queries). GROUND-TRUTH: read internal/wiki/schema.go Page struct (line 61) + parser.go (line 243 Sources field) before adding Aliases; mirror the YAML tag pattern.

Conflict policy verified by test: two pages claim 'Codice' alias → first-write wins by file mtime; the loser is logged as a Lint warning. Longest-prefix policy: 'Codice Civile' (longer) always wins over 'Codice' (shorter) at lookup time even if 'Codice' was indexed first

userStories.title: Alias-aware InjectAcrossWiki using AliasIndex (no regex on prose)
userStories.description: Extend the existing InjectEntityLinks helper (internal/wiki/inject_links.go, shipped 2026-05-23 commit 6aabfbda) to consult the AliasIndex from US-GRAPH-01 in addition to entity titles. Build a unified candidate list = titles ∪ all aliases, all normalized via the same normalization as the index. Matching strategy: literal substring with word-boundary on KNOWN strings (escaped with regexp.QuoteMeta, NOT regex on prose — per memory feedback_no_regex_for_nlp). Sort by candidate-string length DESC so 'Codice Civile' wins over 'Codice' at match site. Inject `[[slug]]` over matched span (preserves original case in the surrounding text). Code fences + existing [[wiki-links]] + HTML comments still masked (the maskProtectedSpans helper from 6aabfbda). Self-link guard preserved. Update InjectAcrossWiki at internal/wiki/inject_links.go (around the candidates loop near line 195) to enumerate aliases from each candidate's frontmatter.

userStories.title: Embedding-based entity dedup pipeline (cosine + LLM tiebreaker)
userStories.description: Build a post-ingest entity-resolution pass that detects + merges near-duplicate entity/concept pages. NOT regex/string-similarity (lift the SCAFFOLD from graphify dedup.py but replace the similarity metric — see memory feedback_no_regex_for_nlp). New file internal/wiki/dedup.go. Algorithm: (1) For each linkable page (entity + concept), compute embedding(title + ' ' + first 200 chars of body). Reuse existing search.EmbeddingFunc from internal/storage/search/qdrant_index.go — same embedder, same dimensions. (2) For each entity, query Qdrant for top-K nearest neighbors (K=10) restricted to category∈{entity,concept}. (3) Cosine pairs: ≥0.92 = auto-merge (high confidence). 0.78–0.92 = enqueue for LLM tiebreaker (a single yes/no Claude call per pair, asking 'are X and Y the same concept in the source domain?'). <0.78 = distinct, no action. (4) Build clusters via Union-Find (lift from graphify dedup.py:UF — 30 LOC trivial port). (5) For each cluster, pick canonical survivor by: most inbound links, then shortest title, then alphabetical. (6) Merge losers into survivor: copy their aliases into survivor's aliases[], rewrite all incoming [[loser]] wikilinks to [[survivor]] in every wiki page body, then DeletePage(loser). (7) Audit log: write merge events to /workspace/wiki/dedup-audit-<ts>.md (cluster, survivor, losers, similarity scores, edge count rewired). Dry-run mode via query param ?dry_run=1 on the trigger endpoint — reports the planned merges without writing. Expose via POST /maintenance/dedup (admin route) AND call from /maintenance/run as final step after InjectAcrossWiki.

Cap at MaxLLMCalls (default 50) — if exceeded, remaining ambiguous pairs flagged as AMBIGUOUS in the report, not merged
Survivor selection: most inbound links (from graph index) wins; tie-break by shortest title; tie-break by alphabetical slug. Losers' aliases appended to survivor's aliases (case-fold dedup)

userStories.notes: DEPENDS ON US-GRAPH-01 (aliases survive merge), US-GRAPH-04 (aliases from extraction). Most expensive story (~400 LOC) but the one that delivers the substrate guarantee. RISK R3: LLM tiebreaker cost — capped at 50 pairs per run, ~$0.05 with Claude Haiku, acceptable for batch operation. RISK R4: false-positive merge of distinct entities with similar embeddings (e.g. 'art. 1218 c.c.' vs 'art. 1218 c.p.' — Codice Civile vs Codice Penale). Mitigation: LLM tiebreaker handles edge cases; raise CosineAutoMerge to 0.95 if false-positives observed in real corpora. RISK R5: deadlock during concurrent WritePage. Mitigation: single global lock with explicit comment + run during maintenance window only.

userStories.title: Typed edges (cites/applies/contradicts/depends_on/...) + colored graph
userStories.description: Replace the generic [[wiki-link]] semantics with explicit edge types so the LLM can express 'sentenza X applies art. 1218' vs 'art. 1218 contradicts art. 2043' vs 'company X depends_on supplier Y'. Three pieces: (a) Extractor schema: ExtractionDelta.Link.Type whitelist EXPANDED from the current 5 ({mentions,uses,extends,contradicts,derived_from}) to a richer set per graphify llm.py:146: {mentions,cites,applies,implements,references,extends,contradicts,depends_on,derived_from,semantically_similar_to}. Prompt updated to explain each type with a one-line example. (b) Wiki body syntax: optional inline type via `[[slug|type]]` (pipe-separated, fallback to 'mentions' when omitted). ExtractWikiLinks parses both `[[slug]]` and `[[slug|type]]`; the in-memory GraphIndex stores edges with type. (c) Frontend WikiGraphView colors edges by type (cites=blue, applies=green, contradicts=red, depends_on=amber, default=gray). Edge legend visible. /api/wiki/graph response gains edge.type field. GROUND-TRUTH: read internal/wiki/schema.go::ExtractWikiLinks (line 234) + internal/wiki/graph_index.go (edges storage) + internal/storage/sources/ingest/extractor.go::ExtractionDelta.Link + web/src/components/WikiGraphView.tsx (edge coloring logic).
